chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Sowrat ibn Kuleyb, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'A woman from our family went out with us, but she was unaware of the Ihram, so she did not enter the state of Ihram until we entered Makkah, and we forgot to instruct her regarding that.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So instruct her, and let her enter the state of Ihram from her place in Makkah or from the Masjid.'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامَ: Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: The Masjid (specifically Masjid al-Haram in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who enters Makkah without Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the flexibility in Hajj jurisprudence for those who enter Makkah without Ihram due to ignorance or forgetfulness, a ruling derived from the principle of ease in religious obligations. The Imam’s instruction to assume Ihram from within the city or the Masjid, rather than requiring a return to the Miqat, underscores the practical application of 'ease' (taysir) in Shia fiqh, distinguishing it from stricter interpretations that might demand re-crossing the boundary. This incident is often cited to demonstrate the leniency granted to travelers who are unaware of the specific Miqat locations or the timing of consecration.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Sowrat Bin Kuleyb who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘I went out (for Hajj) and with us was a woman from our family. She did not know about (wearing of) the Ihraam until we entered Makkah, and we forgot that we should be instructing her with that’. Heasws said: ‘So instruct her, and let her wear Ihraam from her place, from Makkah or from the Masjid’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Sawrah ibn Kulayb who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman of our family who was with us and was ignorant of Ihram, so she did not assume the state of Ihram until we entered Makkah and we forgot to tell her about it. He (the Imam) said, ‘You can instruct her to assume the state of Ihram from wherever she is in Makkah or Masjid.”’
